title: Fully differential two-stage OTA
description: The fully differential version of the two-stage Miller OTA: a differential input stage with current-source loads driving a differential common-source second stage, Miller-compensated with $C_c$ on each side. The small-signal frequency plan is the same as the single-ended Miller OTA — GBW = $g_{m1}/(2*\pi*C_c)$, an RHP zero $z = g_{m2}/C_c$ removed by the $R_z = 1/g_{m2}$ nulling resistor, a second-pole/phase-margin estimate, and SR = $min(I_1/C_c, I_2/C_L)$. Three things genuinely differ in the fully differential form: the stage-1 load is a current source rather than a current mirror, so there is no mirror pole or pole-zero doublet in the signal path (a cleaner frequency response); the differential output swing is twice the single-ended range; and a common-mode feedback loop is needed to set the output common mode, costing supply current. As in the telescopic sheet, the CMFB loop is out of scope (no loop solving) and appears only as the current line item $I_{cmfb}$. The stage-1 output common mode $V_1$ is the node the CMFB loop holds, but it is not a free number: that node is the stage-2 gate, so the loop must hold it exactly one stage-2 $V_{GS}$ from the supply, and the sheet derives it there rather than asking for it. The pole and phase-margin rows are ESTIMATE-grade; the simulator owns stability sign-off. On the demo NMOS table the polarity-inverted devices keep their sign params at +1.

params.name: CL
params.note: output load capacitance (per side)

params.name: PM_target
params.note: phase-margin target; the PM row is estimate-grade

params.name: swing_target
params.note: required differential peak output swing

params.name: C1_est
params.note: stage-1 output node cap; refine from the stage-2 cgg plus extraction

params.name: CM_dc
params.note: the input common mode the application presents. The engine places the tail node so the sheet sits exactly here; sweep it to trace the common-mode axis This sheet carries NO containment edges: stage 1 does not close on sky130-class supplies at these defaults, and a range claim that cannot be tuned honestly would be theater — see the single-stage OTAs for the pattern.

params.name: V_tail
params.note: the input pair's tail node. Solved rather than set: bisected between min and max (the BRACKET) until the produced common mode equals CM_dc. Fixes the pair's body bias and drain-source voltage in one stroke

params.name: I_cmfb
params.note: current the common-mode feedback network draws; the CMFB loop itself is out of scope — supply-budget line item only

params.name: Cc
params.note: Miller compensation cap (per side): sets the dominant pole and GBW = gm1/(2*pi*Cc)

params.name: I1
params.note: stage-1 tail current

params.name: I2
params.note: stage-2 branch current (per side)

params.name: gm_id_in
params.note: input-pair inversion

params.name: gm_id_ld1
params.note: stage-1 load inversion

params.name: gm_id_s2
params.note: stage-2 device inversion

params.name: gm_id_ld2
params.note: stage-2 load inversion

params.name: V_out2
params.note: stage-2 output common-mode DC, set by CMFB

params.name: ld_sign
params.note: vds sign of the load tables: +1 N-style, -1 signed-PMOS

params.name: out_sign
params.note: vds sign of the stage-2 device table: +1 N-style, -1 signed-PMOS

doc.title: Stage-2 common-source device
doc.description: The second-stage gain device (per side) carrying the stage-2 current at the output common mode; its gm sets the RHP zero, second pole, and nulling resistor. Sized FIRST, because its gate-source voltage is what fixes the stage-1 output level the rest of the sheet biases against. Its wiring declaration is TAUTOLOGICAL as the sheet stands: $V_1$ is derived from this device’s own gate-source voltage, so the declared node and the checked node are the same number and the check cannot fire. It is kept because it stops being tautological the moment someone re-types $V_1$ as a plain parameter — which is exactly the defect this mechanism was built after.

params.name: vx
params.note: signed to this table's axis convention

doc.title: Stage-1 current-source load
doc.description: A stage-1 current-source load (not a mirror — this is what removes the mirror pole) carrying half the tail current at the stage-1 output common mode.

params.name: vx
params.note: signed to this table's axis convention. The parent drives it from the supply minus the stage-1 output level, which is the V1 row's expression written out — use params are evaluated before rows, so the level is restated here rather than referenced

doc.title: Stage-1 input-pair device
doc.description: Half-circuit input device at half the tail current; its drain sits at the stage-1 output common mode, its source one vgs below the input common mode.

params.name: vx
params.note: the drain sits at the stage-1 output level and the source at the tail node, so the parent drives this from the V1 row's expression written out — use params are evaluated before rows, so the level is restated here rather than referenced

doc.title: Stage-2 current-source load
doc.description: The second-stage current-source load (per side) carrying the stage-2 current at the output common mode.

rows.name: V1
rows.note: stage-1 output common-mode DC. Derived, not typed: this node IS the stage-2 gate, so the level is whatever the stage-2 device's own gate-source voltage asks for, one vgs below the supply for a p-type stage-2 (abs() keeps both table conventions working). The common-mode feedback loop is what holds the node there — it commands the level, it does not choose it, and typing a different number here is the classic way to starve stage 2. The wiring declaration on the stage-2 use is what keeps the two descriptions of this node in agreement

rows.name: CM_in
rows.note: the input common mode this bias produces — an OUTPUT here, not a setting; rises monotonically with the tail node, so the pin is a well-posed bisection

rows.name: gm2
rows.note: stage-2 transconductance: sets the RHP zero, second pole, and nulling resistor

rows.name: z_rhp
rows.note: the right-half-plane zero the feedforward path through Cc would place, kept as a reference point for the UNCOMPENSATED stage: the Rz = 1/gm2 nulling resistor below moves it to infinity, which is why the phase-margin row carries no zero term

rows.name: p2
rows.note: non-dominant pole ESTIMATE; refine C1_est from the stage-2 cgg plus extraction

rows.name: Rz
rows.note: nulling resistor Rz = 1/gm2 that moves the RHP zero to infinity

rows.name: PM
rows.note: ESTIMATE: crossover phase lag from the second pole alone, because the Rz = 1/gm2 nulling resistor removes the RHP zero. The simulator owns stability sign-off

rows.name: SR
rows.note: the smaller slew limit: stage-1 tail charging Cc, or stage-2 current charging CL

rows.name: Av1
rows.note: stage-1 gain into the input-device and current-source-load output conductances

rows.name: Rout
rows.note: SINGLE-SIDE output resistance: stage two's own output conductance in parallel with its load device's, on one of the two output branches. The differential output resistance a parent loads is twice this, the same half-circuit convention the gain and the input-capacitance rows use. The gain assumes a capacitive load, so nothing here models a resistive one; this row is what a composing parent checks its own loading against

rows.name: Av2
rows.note: stage-2 common-source gain into its own and the load conductances

rows.name: Av
rows.note: two-stage DC gain (product of the stage gains)

rows.name: swing_diff
rows.note: differential output swing = twice the single-ended range set by the two output-device saturation voltages (the fully differential swing doubling)

rows.name: I_total
rows.note: total supply current: two stage-2 branches, the stage-1 tail, and the CMFB network

rows.name: cgg2
rows.note: stage-2 gate capacitance — the dominant term in the stage-1 output cap C1_est

rows.name: cgg_in
rows.note: estimate: the capacitance one input terminal presents — the gate capacitance of a single input device. Gate capacitance only, because the Miller term needs the gate-drain fraction and these tables do not carry it, so a driving stage sees more than this. No rule reads it

rules.note: two-stage DC gain meets the target
the worse of the two slew limits meets the target
the differential output swing meets the target
the compensated bandwidth (gm1/(2*pi*Cc)) meets the target

ESTIMATE-grade phase margin; the simulator owns the real stability sign-off. This is also the sheet’s only check on pole spacing: PM falls as the second pole approaches the crossover, so a design that crowds them fails here rather than needing a separate zero/pole guardrail
